propositions: MCP transition_ticket and claim_ticket signatures omit force, reason, caused_by, and ref parameters that are already supported by the library and CLI, making them unreachable over MCP.

FastMCP derives JSON schemas and argument models from handwritten callable signatures; undeclared payload keys are discarded before the registered callable runs, causing parameter loss at the adapter boundary.
The MCP adapter forwards only close_class for transition and assignee for claim, so even if schema fields were added, the underlying parameters would still be lost without forwarding.
The operator ruling rescinded the force-only-CLI policy; force must be exposed through all surfaces (CLI, library, MCP) with absent certification as the audit signal rather than force_close.
The repair requires adding library-compatible parameters to MCP signatures and forwarding all parameters unchanged to the shared library core without adding new logic or dependencies.
Lifecycle tests through real registered FastMCP tools must validate that reason-required close, caused_by edges, explicit ref targeting, and both force paths persist through the adapter to the core.
